content.comment_body:
SSA-921449: Plaintext Password Storage Vulnerability in [product_name] [version_no] Devices. Published: 2024-08-13. Last updated: 2024-08-13. Current Version: [version_no]. CVSS v3.1 Score: 4.6; CVSS v4.0 Score: 5.1. SUMMARY: Several [company_name] [product_name] [version_no] (including SIPLUS variants) devices are affected by a vulnerability where passwords are stored in plaintext. An attacker with physical access could potentially extract passwords from embedded storage components. [company_name] has released new hardware in the [product_name] [version_no] family that addresses this issue for some devices, and is developing updates for SIPLUS variants. More info is available in "Additional Information" below. 
 Affected Products & Remediation: - [product_name] [version_no]: No current fix planned. See Workarounds and Mitigations. - SIPLUS [product_name] [version_no]: No current fix planned. See Workarounds and Mitigations. 
 Workarounds and Mitigations: - CVE-2024-39922: Ensure physical security to prevent unauthorized access. Reference operational guidelines for Industrial Security (e.g. physical prevention of access to critical infrastructure). - Follow General Security Recommendations. 
 General Security Recommendations: [company_name] recommends protecting device network access appropriately and operating in secure IT environments as outlined in their Industrial Security guidelines ([url]), and to follow recommendations in official product manuals. More information on Industrial Security can be found at: [url]. 
 Vulnerability Description: This vulnerability (CVE-2024-39922) means passwords are stored without protection, so a physical attacker could retrieve them. CVSS v3.1 Score: 4.6. CVSS:3.1/AV:P/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:P/RL:O/RC:C. CVSS v4.0 Score: 5.1. CVSS:4.0/AV:P/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. CWE/CWE-256: Plaintext Password Storage. 
 Additional Information: Hardware revisions in [product_name] [version_no] family address this vulnerability for several devices (examples with [article_no] omitted). Work on SIPLUS variants is in progress. For further inquiries about security vulnerabilities, reach out to [company_name] ProductCERT: [url]. 
 HISTORY: V1.0 (2024-08-13): Initial release. Terms of Use: All [company_name] Security Advisories are subject to [company_name]'s license terms or other suitable agreements. The Terms of Use for [company_name]'s website ([url]) apply in addition. License Terms prevail if there are conflicts. SSA-921449 ©[company_name] 2024.

analysis.insight_summary: The primary concern described is the security vulnerability in [product_name] [version_no] devices, which store passwords in an unprotected, plaintext format. Attackers with physical access may retrieve these passwords without difficulty. No direct fix is available for current hardware, with only mitigation guidance provided. Users must rely on best practices and physical safeguards until new, more secure hardware versions are released.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect secure password handling in [product_name] [version_no] devices and are seeking direct technical solutions or updates to address the vulnerability in existing hardware, rather than just receiving advice or mitigation steps.
pain_keywords: lack of update for old hardware
